newsitem.title: IRAQ: Kurdish faction takes Iraqi town from rivals.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish faction takes Iraqi town from rivals.

text.p: Fighters of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) on Friday overwhelmed a rival Kurdish militia group and seized the strategic northern Iraqi town of Koy Sanjak after heavy fighting, witnesses said.

Guerrillas cheered and waved yellow KDP flags in the town after forces from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) fled to the nearby Heibet Sultan mountain under a fierce bomardment of artillery and Katyusha rockets.
There did not appear to be many casualties. The KDP's radio station blared out martial music to celebrate the victory.
The fall of Koy Sanjak broke a partial PUK seige of the city of Arbil, northern Iraq's administrative centre that was taken by the KDP fighting with Iraqi government forces in late August.
The United States has urged the two warring Kurdish factions to call an immediate ceasefire.
The KDP earlier said it would halt its push once it had taken Koy Sanjak and given Arbil a breather from days of PUK pressure.

"Today we want to enter Koy Sanjak, continue to Heibet Sultan mountain and then stop," local KDP commander Arif Tayfur told Reuters in the town of Degala, near the front line, before the assault on Koy Sanjak.
The PUK, led by Jalal Talabani, this week closed in on Arbil from several points, the closest being Degala 30 km (20 miles) to the south.
The status of Arbil, a city of 800,000 people and symbol of Kurdish autonomy hopes, could be key to peace negotiations.

KDP leader Massoud Barzani is due to meet Robert Pelletreau, U.S. assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs, next week for talks on ending the Kurdish feud. The meeting is likely to be in Turkey.
